title: Purification of DNA repair protein complexes from mammalian cells
protocol: Clone human FANCD2 cDNA into the pOZ-N retroviral expression vector containing Flag and HA tags at the N-terminus.
Use CRISPR/Cas9 to introduce FLAG-HA tag into the FANCD2 gene in its chromosomal location.
Seed 120,000 Phoenix-A cells in one well of a 6-well plate or a 6-cm dish for transfection.
Prepare the DNA mixture containing target plasmids and two helper plasmids in Tube No 1.
Pipette the DNA mixture from Tube No 1 into Tube No 2, invert 5 times, and incubate at 20–25°C for 15–30 minutes.
Pipette the transfection mixture drop-wise into the well with Phoenix-A cells.
Gently rock the plate to help disperse the transfection mixture.
Let the cells grow for 66–72 hours.
Harvest the retrovirus and pass the supernatant through a 0.22 μm filter.
Assess expression level of protein of interest by SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting with specific antibodies after harvesting Phoenix-A cells.
Prepare 30 mL of 0.1% FBS in PBS (referred to as PBS/FBS).
Aliquot 1.8 mL of Dynabeads Goat Anti-Mouse IgG Magnetic Beads into three 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes (600 μL each).
Place the tubes on a magnetic stand for 2 minutes.
Remove the supernatant gently after placing the tubes on a magnetic stand.
Resuspend the beads with 1 mL PBS/FBS gently.
Repeat the magnetic capturing and washing twice.
Gently resuspend the beads with 600 μL PBS/FBS after the last wash.
Dissolve 200 μg of lyophilized anti-IL-2Rα antibody (whole vial) with 600 μL of PBS/FBS.
Transfer 20 μL to a separate tube for later SDS-PAGE analysis as an input sample.
Add 200 μL of anti-IL-2Rα antibody to each tube of beads.
Incubate the tubes on a slow rotator in the cold room for 12–16 hours.
Place the tubes on a magnetic stand for 2 minutes.
Gently transfer the supernatant to a 15-mL tube as "flow through."
Remove the tubes from the magnetic stand.
Gently resuspend the beads with 1 mL PBS/FBS.
Repeat the magnetic capturing and washing three times without keeping the supernatant.
For each tube, resuspend the beads in 1 mL PBS/FBS supplemented with 50% glycerol as "coupled beads."
Aliquot the beads in 200 μL per 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Store the beads at −20°C.
Analyze “input,” “flow through” and “coupled beads” by SDS-PAGE followed by Coomassie stain.
Detach HeLa S3 cells by treating with PBS supplemented with 2 mM EDTA.
Pellet down roughly 200,000 cells in a 15 mL tube at 188 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C.
Resuspend the cells with the retrovirus stock.
Plate the cell-virus mixture in a 9 cm dish.
Let the cells grow in the virus stock overnight (less than 24 hours).
Collect and centrifuge the supernatant at 188 × g, 20°C, for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend the cell pellet with fresh supplemented DMEM, and plate the cells back in a 9 cm dish.
Allow the cells to grow until they reach 60%–80% confluency (66–72 hours).
Detach the transduced HeLa S3 cells by treating them with PBS supplemented with 2 mM EDTA.
Centrifuge the cells at 188 × g, 20°C, for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 1 mL of fresh supplemented DMEM in a 1.5 mL microtube.
Add 10 μL of 50% slurry IL-2Rα antibody conjugated magnetic beads to the cells.
Leave the tube on a roller at 20–25°C for 1 hour.
Place the tube on a magnetic stand for 2 minutes.
Gently remove the supernatant after placing it on the magnetic stand.
Remove the tube from the magnetic stand and gently resuspend the cells with the beads using 1 mL of fresh DMEM.
Repeat the magnetic capturing and washing process twice more.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of supplemented DMEM and plate them into a 9 cm dish containing 9 mL of supplemented DMEM.

Grow HeLa S3 cells as suspension cultures in spinner flasks at 37°C using Joklik’s Modified MEM supplemented with 2.5% FBS, 2 mM L-glutamine, non-essential amino acids (100× dilution), and penicillin-streptomycin (100× dilution).
Detach HeLa S3 cells from an 80% confluent dish.
Centrifuge the detached cells.
Resuspend the cells in supplemented Joklik’s medium at a concentration suitable for growth in spinner flasks.
Expand the culture by adding an equal volume of fresh supplemented Joklik’s medium to the flask or transferring it to a larger spinner flask.
Monitor the color change of the medium, ensuring it changes to orange but not yellow over time.
Double the volume of the culture each day until the desired scale is reached.
Treat the cells with 160 ng/mL Mitomycin C for 16 h.
Harvest the cells by centrifuging the culture at 1,800 × g, 4°C for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash the cell pellet by resuspending it in 50 mL cold PBS.
Centrifuge (1,800 × g, 4°C) and discard the supernatant.
Equilibrate the cell pellet with hypotonic buffer by resuspending the pellet in 2 mL of hypotonic buffer.
Centrifuge (1,800 × g, 4°C) and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend and incubate the pellet in 4 mL of hypotonic buffer on ice for 10 min.
Use a B type tight pestle with a clearance of 20–56 μm to homogenize samples promptly and steadily for 10–20 cycles on ice.
Collect samples before and after homogenization to examine under a microscope.
Continue homogenization until cell membrane rupture efficiency is above 90%.
Centrifuge the solution at 3,300 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C to pellet nuclei.
Insert a clean pipette tip into the solution to remove the top lipid layer adhering to it.
Collect the supernatant as the cytoplasmic fraction and supplement with 11% of its volume in 10× S-100 buffer.
Centrifuge the supplemented cytoplasmic fraction at 17,000 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the lipid layer from the centrifuged cytoplasmic fraction using a clean pipette tip.
Resuspend nuclei in 1 mL low-salt NE buffer supplemented with 0.01% Triton X-100 and 75 unit/mL Benzonase, and incubate on ice for 30 min.
Supplement the mixture with formaldehyde to achieve a final concentration of 1%, and incubate at 20–25°C for 4 min.
Quench the formaldehyde by adding 150 μL of 2.5 M Glycine pH 7.5.
Centrifuge the mixture (3,000 × g, 4°C, 10 min) and discard the supernatant.
Wash crosslinked nuclei with 10 mL PBS, centrifuge at 3,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C, and discard the supernatant.
Repeat washing step twice more.
Resuspend crosslinked nuclei in 1 mL high-salt NE buffer.
Sonicate the crosslinked nuclei for 20 min with 1 s on/off intervals at 4 W power in an ice/water slurry bath.
Sonicate chromatin DNA to render it into smaller fragments.
Incubate sonicated nuclei on ice for 30 minutes.
Dilute the lysate 5-fold with 8 mL of low-salt NE buffer supplemented with 125 mM NaCl and 1% Tween 20.
Centrifuge the solution at 17,000 × g at 4°C for 20 minutes.
Collect the supernatant as nuclear extract.
Snap-freeze the nuclear extract using liquid nitrogen.
Store the snap-frozen nuclear extract at -80°C for later purification.
Add 250 μl bed volume of anti-FLAG M2 agarose beads to the 10 ml nuclear extract.
Incubate the tube on a rotator at 10 rpm for 1.5–2 h at 4°C.
Wash anti-FLAG M2 agarose beads with 5 column volumes (c.v.) of 100 mM glycine pH 2.5.
Wash anti-FLAG M2 agarose beads with 10 c.v. of ddH2O.
Wash anti-FLAG M2 agarose beads with 10 c.v. of buffer A.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1,000 × g for 4°C and 5 minutes to collect supernatant as flow-through fraction.
Resuspend washed beads in 1 mL of Buffer A and transfer them to a clean gravity-flow chromatography column.
Apply 10 ml of Buffer A to wash beads, repeating the washing step two more times.
Cap the outlet during buffer application to allow efficient dripping through before applying more buffer.
Add 250 μL of Buffer A supplemented with 0.5 mg/mL FLAG peptide to anti-FLAG beads in the column.
Seal the top with parafilm and leave the column on a roller at 4°C for 1 hour.
Perform the elution in batch using FLAG peptide to efficiently compete away FLAG-tagged FANCD2 from anti-FLAG beads.
Collect the FLAG eluate and repeat the elution once more.
Pool all collected FLAG eluates.
Add 60 μl bed volume of anti-HA Sepharose beads to the pooled FLAG eluate, then incubate at 10 rpm for 2 h at 4°C.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C and collect the supernatant as the flow-through fraction of the anti-HA purification step.
Apply 5 mL Buffer A to wash the beads.
Repeat the washing step two more times.
Cap the outlet and apply 60 μL of Buffer A supplemented with 0.5 mg/mL HA peptide.
Seal the top with parafilm.
Leave the column on a roller at 4°C for 1 hour.
Elute the protein complexes from the anti-HA Sepharose matrix using 0.1 M Glycine pH 2.5.
Add 1/5 volume of 1.5 M Tris pH 8.8 to neutralize the eluate immediately after collecting it.
Collect the HA eluate.
Repeat the elution once more.
Revert formaldehyde crosslinks and prepare samples for mass spectrometry analysis.
Supplement the HA eluate with 0.1% SDS and 5 mM DTT and incubate the sample at 95°C for 20 min to reverse formaldehyde crosslinks.
Dilute the sample ten-fold with milli-Q water supplemented with 5 mM DTT and cool on ice for 5 min.
Supplement the sample with 15 mM Iodoacetamide and incubate at 20-25°C protected from light for 20 min.
Supplement the sample with 10 mM of DTT and incubate at 20-25°C protected from light for 15 min.
Mix equal volume of sample with 20% TCA to supplement the sample with 10% TCA and incubate on ice 2–16 h, protected from light.
Centrifuge the sample at 17,000 × g at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Rinse the pellet gently with −20°C 100% acetone.
Centrifuge the sample at 17,000 × g at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Let the pellet air-dry at 20–25°C.
Analyze the precipitated protein complexes by MS/MS.
